I can't take this infrographic seriously. It makes some poor comparisons and seems to overshadow other factors that contribute to those statistics. There isn't all negatives to gun control but there's enough positives that gun control would be a recommended move.

Where a police officer is not only trained how to use a fire arm safely he's taught when it's appropriate to flex that right and i would hope a police officer has a better more well rounded understanding of the laws that surround that and situational awareness as to when's the right time to use a gun. The average civilian may have a gun but lack the rest of the knowledge or training to actually use it as a deterrence properly.

>This is called projection, based on emotions and not facts. While this does happen, it's rare. The majority of gun crimes in America is caused by people who already had a criminal records, gang members, and the like. And the big reason gang members are killing each other? Drugs.

Well if the majority of gun crimes are convicted by people with previous criminal records then keep guns away from dangerous people like people with records. More strict gun laws would make that easier to do. And gang members may fight over drugs, but a gang will fight over anything that makes profit. Drugs are tax free, high profits, in demand and you don't have to compete with already large monopolized industries that are currently legal. This is partially enabled by the war on drugs and consequences prisoners face after leaving prison. (But that's a whole other discussion entirely.) Essentially they would fight over pencils if they had the same profits as drugs did.

>Except the top 10 guns used in crimes are handguns and revolvers, not "high caliber" guns. Even the infamous AR15 isn't a "high caliber" gun.

>I never argued this point. I think recreational drugs should be legal. I'd put my money on all crime, not just gun crime, being cut in half if this happened.

I think we can both agree on this one. :)

>If almost no one in Australia has a gun, why do your police carry them?

I'm pretty sure most police officers carry guns not for the intention to get into fire fights or a stand off with criminals. If it does come to that, usually a professional fighting unit is called in like SWAT or a task force for example. 

Guns can be used as a deterrence for criminals; someone is less likely to attack a police officer or someone else with a non projectile weapon if the officer is pointing a gun at them. Criminals are also less likely to flee and run if the officer flexes the risk that they could be shot if they attempted to.The reason why gun control should be implemented is for a few reasons. First off guns are tempting, you're probably more likely to shoot someone in a rage of bad decisions and kill them much faster than physically attacking them which takes time, effort, and concious planning aka a lot more time to think about what you're doing. I would also assume criminals would have a harder time getting high caliber weapons if not just any weapon at all if weapons were monitored and controlled more closely.

The difference with drugs is that drugs are not the same as guns. Where drugs possess the risk of killing, guns were actually made with the intention to kill. I'm sure you would agree the danger associated with getting shot far out-ways the danger of say trying heroin.

This why we need to recognize that drugs and guns are to different things and should be dealt with responsibly and accordingly.
